body.statement: Let \(\widetilde Q\) be any finite signed unit-mass measure on \(\mathcal Y\), let \(G_{\varepsilon}\subset\mathcal Y\) be a finite grid of mesh at most \(\varepsilon\), and let \(\Pi_{\varepsilon}(\widetilde Q)\) minimize the Kantorovich--Rubinstein distance from \(\widetilde Q\) over probability measures supported on \(G_{\varepsilon}\). Then for every probability law \(\mu\) on \(\mathcal Y\), \(W_1\{\Pi_{\varepsilon}(\widetilde Q),\mu\}\le2\lVert\widetilde Q-\mu\rVert_{\mathrm{KR}}+C_m\varepsilon\). A finite linear program with deterministic tie-breaking computes the projection and its masses define an executable categorical sampler.
body.justification: Higher-order coefficient correction can be signed, so an order-preserving projection theorem is needed to deliver an actual generative distribution.
body.gap: NilesWeedBerthet2022 projects direct-sample wavelet estimates to densities or discrete measures; the present statement isolates a finite-grid signed-input oracle inequality suitable after causal higher-order correction.
body.consumer: The known-design reconstruction benchmark can return probability masses and sample categorically without clipping away multiscale cancellation.
